query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases is governed by the selective oxidation or reduction of specific elements (e.g., Al or Ti), leading to the formation of brittle oxide or intermetallic phases at grain boundaries, which may cause catastrophic failure due to grain boundary embrittlement.
generation.material_initial_state: Additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by reducing the Al and Ti content by 10% each, while maintaining the overall high-entropy alloy composition.
generation.conditions: Elevated-temperature exposure (e.g., 800–1000°C) in oxidizing (e.g., air or oxygen-rich) or reducing (e.g., hydrogen-rich) gas environments for up to 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of brittle oxide or intermetallic phases at grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Selective oxidation or reduction of Al and Ti at elevated temperatures leads to the formation of brittle phases, which weaken grain boundaries and promote crack initiation and propagation under thermal or mechanical stress.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy with reduced Al and Ti content will exhibit reduced grain boundary embrittlement and improved resistance to catastrophic failure compared to the baseline alloy under identical exposure conditions.
generation.baseline: The original Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, which is expected to show significant grain boundary embrittlement and a higher likelihood of catastrophic failure under the specified conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is applicable within the temperature range of 800–1000°C and in oxidizing or reducing gas environments. It may not apply to non-gaseous environments or temperatures outside this range.
generation.uncertainty: The specific role of Al and Ti in grain boundary embrittlement and the exact nature of the brittle phases formed are not fully understood and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose both the baseline and modified alloys to identical elevated-temperature conditions in oxidizing and reducing gas environments. Perform microstructural analysis (e.g., SEM, TEM, EDS) to identify grain boundary phases and mechanical testing (e.g., tensile or creep tests) to assess failure modes.
measurements: Grain boundary composition and phase identification
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified alloy with reduced Al and Ti content exhibits similar or worse grain boundary embrittlement and failure behavior compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis will be falsified.
